DSP mock B

Instructions

  • Time allowed: 2 hours. Sit it in one go, timed, with your printed notes, Test 1 Reference and reference sheet beside you (open book, hard copy only).
  • Attempt all 11 questions. There are 60 marks in total. Marks for each part are given in brackets. Budget about 2 minutes per mark, and keep the last 5 minutes to check.
  • Show your working. Most marks go to method, so a wrong number with a correct method still scores.
  • Some parts say “assuming the answer to part (x) is …”. Use the value given there, even if your own answer is different. This stops one slip from costing you the rest of the question.
  • Notation is the course’s. is DT frequency (rad/sample), is CT frequency (rad/s). . The arrow marks the sample. Use for every bilinear-transform calculation.
  • This paper is meant to feel different from mock A. It uses the less common angles of L03–L10. Do not open the marking guide until time is up.

Marks: (a) 1. (b) 1 for correct blocks with the 2-sample overlap. (c) 2 for the block outputs (½ each), 1 for the assembled . (d) 1 with a reason.

Common mistakes

  • Confusing the two methods. Overlap-save overlaps the inputs and discards outputs. Overlap-add uses non-overlapping input blocks and adds the overlapping output tails.
  • Forgetting the leading zeros, so the first block has nothing to discard.
  • Stopping after 3 blocks and losing the last two output samples (5, 2).
  • Keeping the first outputs instead of the last .

Reread: D6 (block convolution, overlap-save and overlap-add).

Question 11: Short answers [4]

Solution

(a) [1] The ideal LPF has (T9 Q1). It is noncausal ( for ), and it is of infinite duration, so it cannot be computed with finite memory and operations. (It is also not absolutely summable.) ½ mark per reason.

(b) [2]

  • Bin spacing: .
  • Resolution is set by the record length, not by : . This is greater than the 50 Hz spacing, so the tones cannot be resolved. Zero padding only interpolates the same smeared spectrum (a simulation shows one peak near 1026 Hz).
  • Minimum record: samples, so .

Marks: ½ for the bin spacing, 1 for “no” with a reason, ½ for and .

(c) [1] The bilinear map gives rad . That corresponds to , not 2500 Hz. The map is nonlinear (frequency warping): the whole axis is squeezed onto , and maps to . That is why the critical edges must be prewarped with .

Common mistakes

  • Saying zero padding “improves resolution”. It improves how finely you sample the DTFT, not your ability to separate tones. The lecture’s wording (“better resolution for sampled DTFT”) means the finer sampling only.
  • Saying the ideal LPF is unstable or has infinite gain. The course’s two reasons are causality and infinite length.

Reread: D6 (frequency analysis with the DFT), D11 (warping), D12 (ideal LPF and windows).
